title: Start reading
subtitle: Pick how you want to read, then just toss me the story.
step.0.title: Style
step.1.title: Story
step.2.title: Options
mode.dehydrate.label: Rewrite & polish
mode.dehydrate.description: Rewrites it to read noticeably better — strips the filler, fixes the grammar, and polishes the prose.
mode.interactive.label: Interactive reading
mode.interactive.description: You steer the story — pick the branches and pivotal moments yourself. Just watch your step: the plot doesn't pull its punches.
capability.title: Agent Models
capability.simple.hint: Although this can be a lighter model, it compresses the cumulative outline across the whole book — a larger context window materially helps coherence.
capability.explain.context: Larger context windows let the agent process more chapters per pass, improving outline coherence and rewrite quality.
capability.explain.capability: Stronger models produce better results — capability matters as much as context size.
capability.defaultBadge: Default — set the real limit in Settings
capability.notConfigured.title: Models not configured
capability.notConfigured.body: Configure at least one model before starting. The dehydrate pipeline needs both a complex and a simple model.
novel.file.label: Upload a text file
novel.internet.label: Find it online
novel.internet.title.label: Story title
novel.internet.author.label: Author (optional)
novel.internet.source.label: Source
novel.internet.source.placeholder: Paste a link, or drop a hint on where to find it.
novel.internet.source.tooltip: Tell me where to read it — a link, a search hint, anything that points the way. It has to be live text on a web page I can open and read, not text baked into an image or a PDF/TXT I'd have to download.
novel.internet.source.hint: Live web text only — no image-locked text, no PDFs or TXT downloads.
novel.source.recommendFile.note: Uploading the file is recommended: it's faster, and unlocks file-only features — table-of-contents navigation, cross-chapter processing (which patterns are repeating, which lore was already explained), and more. Internet fetch streams one chapter at a time with no cross-chapter context, so those features stay disabled.
options.dehydrate.basic.grammarFix.label: Typos, grammar & punctuation neat-freak
options.dehydrate.basic.grammarFix.toolt: Zero tolerance for typos, mangled grammar, or rogue punctuation — half-matched quotes, orphaned brackets, the works. Reads like it never met a copyeditor? Not anymore.
options.dehydrate.basic.webSlangFilter.l: Filter cringe clichés & undo the censoring
options.dehydrate.basic.webSlangFilter.t: Burned out on 'let out a breath they didn't know they were holding', 'a shiver ran down their spine', and 'could cut the tension with a knife'? Plus all that asterisk-mangled censoring? We're cleaning house — fresh prose in, tired tropes and broken words out.
options.section.cleanup.title: Cleanup
options.section.situation.title: Dehydrate by scenario
options.section.situation.hint: Toggle the exact filler patterns you want stripped. Keeps the plot, characters, payoffs, and foreshadowing intact — only compresses repetition and low-information content.
options.situation.enforcement.note: These checkboxes are optional enforcement — come back and tick one only when a pattern keeps slipping through. Leave them all off by default: the strength dial alone usually dehydrates intelligently. Too many ticks just becomes noise.
options.situation.strength.label: Dehydrate & accelerate
options.situation.strength.tooltip: Sets how hard the situational tactics are stripped. Off = no situational dehydration at all; Light/Medium/Heavy drives intelligent dehydration even with nothing checked below.
options.section.crossChapter.title: Cross-chapter
options.section.crossChapter.hint: These patterns can only be judged across chapters (e.g. whether a setting was already explained earlier, or whether a beat is repeating). Toggle the ones you want stripped — this is a placeholder for now; the backend doesn't run cross-chapter processing yet, so it won't take effect.
options.crossChapter.enforcement.note: These checkboxes are optional enforcement — come back and tick one only when a pattern keeps slipping through. Leave them all off by default: the strength dial alone usually dehydrates intelligently. Too many ticks just becomes noise.
options.crossChapter.strength.label: Dehydrate & accelerate
options.crossChapter.strength.tooltip: Sets how hard the cross-chapter tactics are stripped. Off = no cross-chapter processing at all; Light/Medium/Heavy drives intelligent dehydration even with nothing checked below.
options.crossChapter.disabled.hint: Cross-chapter processing needs access to multiple chapters at once to judge them together. It's only available when you upload a file — not for internet fetch or non-chaptered sources.
options.section.rewrite.title: Rewrite intensity
options.section.rewrite.hint: Each aspect only applies above Off. Off = skip it; Light / Medium / Heavy = how hard it pushes.
options.section.language.title: Language & translation
options.section.language.tooltip: Optional language transforms — independent, so turn on only what you want; the reader reconciles the rest.
options.section.custom.title: Custom instructions
options.dehydrate.depth.dialoguePacing.t: Tightens the back-and-forth of dialogue so it snaps instead of dragging. Higher = more aggressive trimming and repatterning of speech beats.
options.dehydrate.depth.dialoguePacing.e: e.g. turning a flat 'He said. She said. He said again.' into a punchy exchange.
options.dehydrate.depth.sceneEnhance.too: Strengthens place and mood — sensory texture, atmosphere, staging. Higher = richer, more immersive scene-building.
options.dehydrate.depth.sceneEnhance.exa: e.g. turning 'It was a dark room' into something you can actually feel.
options.dehydrate.depth.combatEnhance.to: Punches up fights and set-pieces — impact, pacing, the 'hell yes' beat. Higher = more cinematic and kinetic.
options.dehydrate.depth.combatEnhance.ex: e.g. making a blow-by-blow clash feel weighty instead of clinical.
options.dehydrate.depth.emotionEnhance.t: Deepens feeling and tension — what characters show, hide, and feel. Higher = more intense emotional texture.
options.dehydrate.depth.emotionEnhance.e: e.g. turning 'She was sad' into a proper gut-punch.
Polishes the prose itself — rhythm, word choice, sentence flow. Higher = more stylistic refinement.
e.g. lifting competent sentences into ones that sing.
options.interactive.frequency.label: Interaction frequency
options.source.nonNovel.label: Not chaptered fiction
options.source.nonNovel.tooltip: Turn this on when your source is one continuous block of text that isn't chaptered fiction — a long Reddit post, a blog article, an email thread, a forum thread, and so on. By default the reader assumes chaptered fiction and pulls each chapter from its own page (or splits a file by its chapter markers). With this on, it treats the whole source as a single storyline and writes the chapters itself, breaking the narrative into organic, evenly-paced chapters along the story's natural beats — not wherever the original happened to break pages. Use it whenever there are no real chapters to parse.
options.source.nonNovel.example: e.g. turning a 5-part Reddit post or a back-and-forth email thread into a proper chaptered read.
options.language.targetLanguage.placehol: A translation instruction like 'translate Latin and Old English into Modern English', or a target language like 简体中文、English、日本語、한국어.
options.language.targetLanguage.label: Translation instruction or target language
options.language.translate.label: Translate
options.language.translate.tooltip: Translates fiction per the instruction or target language you type in once it's on. Most readers won't need this — leave it off if you already read the original.
options.language.translate.example: e.g. reading Russian fiction in English without losing the story.
options.language.nameLocalization.label: Localize names
options.language.nameLocalization.toolti: Reworks character and place names so they read naturally in the target language — fixes tongue-twisting transliterations and unreadable romanizations.
options.language.nameLocalization.exampl: e.g. taming a tangle of romanized pinyin names from Chinese or romaji names from Japansee into ones you can actually keep straight.
options.language.dialogueSubject.label: Restore dialogue subjects
options.language.dialogueSubject.tooltip: Japanese fictions often drop the subject and signal the speaker with verbal tics alone. This re-adds clear attribution so you always know who's talking.
options.language.dialogueSubject.example: e.g. turning a tic-laced line into '…,' she said, flicking her hair.
options.customInstruction.label: Anything else to tweak?
options.customInstruction.placeholder: Change it however you like — just tell me.
options.customInstruction.tooltip: Put any instruction you'd like to add that is not included in the options above. Make sure this doesn't conflict with the options above.
terms.label: I agree to the usage terms
terms.body: I will use this software in accordance with the laws of my jurisdiction and only access content I have the right to read. Contents are fetched from third-party websites or provided by the user; this software does not host, control, or endorse that content and is not responsible for it. options.tactic.tournamentLoop.label: Tournament / ranking loops
options.tactic.tournamentLoop.tooltip: Arena tours, ranking tournaments, league and talent matches padding the bout count with no-name undercards. Keeps only fights involving the protagonist or main-line resources; compresses the rest to a one-line result.
options.tactic.mobGrinding.label: Mob / minion grinding
options.tactic.mobGrinding.tooltip: Wave after wave of samey mobs, zombies, bugs, or assassins differing only in name and color. Merges samey enemies; keeps only the first-threat, key-resource, or bigger-enemy-triggering fight.
options.tactic.combatFrameByFrame.label: Frame-by-frame combat
options.tactic.combatFrameByFrame.toolti: One punch dissected into gathering qi, robes whipping, air trembling, onlookers paling — two thousand words for a single blow. Compresses to 'key action — impact — consequence'.
options.tactic.skillNameSpam.label: Skill-name spam
options.tactic.skillNameSpam.tooltip: Endless recaps of move names ('Ninefold Thunder Art, third turn, Dragon-Break') plus their history, potency, cost, and counter. Keeps the name and core effect on first appearance; later uses get a short tag or just the result.
options.tactic.powerLevelLecture.label: Power-level lectures
options.tactic.powerLevelLecture.tooltip: Re-explaining qi-refining / foundation / golden-core tiers, F-to-SSS ranks, bronze-to-gold grades at every new map. Keeps only what the current conflict needs; never re-lectures an already-explained system.
options.tactic.fakeDisadvantage.label: Fake 'he's losing' tension
options.tactic.fakeDisadvantage.tooltip: The protagonist has a trump card, yet we loop 'pinned down — friends worry — villain gloats — protagonist smirks'. Compresses the loop; gets to and sharpens the reversal sooner.
options.tactic.escalatingElders.label: Escalating elders
options.tactic.escalatingElders.tooltip: Beat the disciple, the elder shows up; beat the elder, the patriarch shows up — nested 'protective elder' escalation. Merges samey tiers; keeps only the escalations that change the conflict's scale or force a new choice.
options.tactic.crowdShock.label: Onlooker shock
options.tactic.crowdShock.tooltip: The crowd gasps, dead silence, 'how is that possible?'. Collapses samey reactions to a line or two; keeps only beats that reflect the protagonist's power or shift opinion.
options.tactic.bystanderExposition.label: Bystander exposition
options.tactic.bystanderExposition.toolt: Two onlookers explaining the backstory ('You don't know? This is the one who…'). Turns necessary info into brief narration; cuts the broadcast voice.
options.tactic.groupPsychology.label: Group psychology
options.tactic.groupPsychology.tooltip: 'Everyone thought he'd lose / she wasn't good enough / he'd gone mad,' re-described over and over. Keeps the core verdict; merges repeated opinions into one line.
options.tactic.danmakuSpam.label: Danmaku / comment spam
options.tactic.danmakuSpam.tooltip: Half a chapter of 'HAHAHA,' 'slay queen,' 'haters take a seat.' Keeps the few comments that mark a real opinion shift; cuts the spam.
options.tactic.mediaReports.label: News / press-release filler
options.tactic.mediaReports.tooltip: 'Shocking!,' 'insiders say,' 'experts believe.' Keeps only the headline, conclusion, or public-opinion fallout that actually affects the plot.
options.tactic.worldbuildingEncyclopedia: Cultivation maps, empires, star sectors, sect tiers, mecha tech trees. Follows 'mention it when it matters'; compresses or cuts everything the current plot doesn't need.
options.tactic.itemProfiles.label: Item / treasure profiles
options.tactic.itemProfiles.tooltip: 'This is Mystic Yin Marrow, from the northern ice plains, one drop a century…'. Keeps only the name, current use, scarcity, and the conflict it causes.
options.tactic.mapTours.label: Map tours
options.tactic.mapTours.tooltip: Every new city: layout, bustling streets, the major factions, local color. Keeps only the places, factions, and dangers the protagonist is about to engage with.
options.tactic.genealogy.label: Family / sect genealogy
options.tactic.genealogy.tooltip: Listing the patriarch, first elder, second elder, main vs. branch lines, who hates whom. Keeps only the relationships the current conflict actually involves.
options.tactic.cultivationRoutine.label: Cultivation routine
options.tactic.cultivationRoutine.toolti: Qi enters the body, courses the meridians, strikes the acupoints, dantian trembles, heavenly portents, breakthrough. Compresses the repeated flow into 'difficulty — method — result/cost'.
options.tactic.systemPanels.label: System / stat panels
options.tactic.systemPanels.tooltip: Re-printing the full sheet — level, strength, agility, skills, points — on every level-up. Shows only the changes that affect the next action.
options.tactic.gachaCheckin.label: Gacha / check-in / loot boxes
options.tactic.gachaCheckin.tooltip: 'Ding! Congratulations, host…' — junk pulls, quips, system explanations, another pull, a flash of gold. Compresses the empty pulls and system chatter.
options.tactic.misunderstandings.label: Misunderstanding tug-of-war
options.tactic.misunderstandings.tooltip: Half-overheard lines, no one explains, friends intervene, a thirty-chapter cold war. When it's just 'nobody explains' stalling the plot, compress it and get the characters moving.
options.tactic.innerMonologueLoop.label: Looping inner monologue
options.tactic.innerMonologueLoop.toolti: 'Does he like me? No way. But just now…' — half a chapter on a single glance. Merges the same feelings into one clear conclusion.
options.tactic.jealousyCycles.label: Jealousy cycles
options.tactic.jealousyCycles.tooltip: An ex / childhood friend / first love shows up → misunderstanding, cold shoulder, interrogation, tension up a notch. Keeps only the beats that advance the relationship or reveal a real need.
options.tactic.outfitDescriptions.label: Outfit / makeup descriptions
options.tactic.outfitDescriptions.toolti: Gown fabric, hairstyle, makeup, jewelry, heels, gasps of awe. Keeps the two or three most distinctive details and their social effect.
options.tactic.banquetFiller.label: Banquets / balls / palace feasts
options.tactic.banquetFiller.tooltip: Entry order, reactions, who disdains whom, gifts, performances, face-slaps, proposals. Prioritizes the core conflict, the probing, the identity reveal, and the relationship shift.
options.tactic.familyGossip.label: Family / relative gossip
options.tactic.familyGossip.tooltip: In-law friction, sisters-in-law, splitting the household, dowries, village chatter, cousins borrowing money. Keeps only the conflicts that change the protagonist's situation, resources, reputation, or feelings.
options.tactic.appearanceRedescription.t: Every entrance re-praises the brows, lips, aura, figure from scratch. Keeps a vivid image on first appearance; later, only notes what changed for the scene.
options.tactic.villainMockery.label: Villain mockery buildup
options.tactic.villainMockery.tooltip: The villain mocks, onlookers pile on, relatives and rivals pile on, stretching it before the face-slap. Keeps the one or two lines that frame the conflict; routes quickly into the comeback.
options.tactic.braindeadVillains.label: Brain-dead villains on repeat
options.tactic.braindeadVillains.tooltip: 'Last time was a fluke!' 'This time he's dead!' — never learning. Compresses the boasts; if there's no new plan, merges it into a single defeat.
options.tactic.narratedConspiracy.label: Narrated end-to-end conspiracy
options.tactic.narratedConspiracy.toolti: The villain's plan narrated in full: motive, steps, personnel, 'foolproof.' Keeps only the key motive and a dangerous step or two; leaves what action can reveal for later.
options.tactic.trialReveal.label: Trial / reveal / confrontation
options.tactic.trialReveal.tooltip: Witnesses, exhibits, CCTV, recordings, texts, testimony flipping and flipping again. Merges repeated testimony; runs the chain as 'misleading evidence — key twist — decisive evidence.'
options.tactic.mealDescriptions.label: Meal descriptions
options.tactic.mealDescriptions.tooltip: Sourcing ingredients, prep, the wok, the aroma, the first bite, the recipe. Outside food-centric stories, keeps only the relationship shift, resource beat, or emotional relief.
options.tactic.travelFiller.label: Travel / journeys
options.tactic.travelFiller.tooltip: Hard mountain roads, weather, meeting merchants, towns, bandits, inn small talk. Compresses repeated terrain and chatter; keeps encounters and foreshadowing.
options.tactic.shoppingFiller.label: Shopping / spending
options.tactic.shoppingFiller.tooltip: Entering a store, snubbed by staff, card-slap face-slap, buying clothes, cars, houses, jewels. Keeps only purchases that spark conflict or move the relationship.
options.tactic.questDungeon.label: Quests / dungeons
options.tactic.questDungeon.tooltip: Take the quest, read the brief, prep items, trash mobs, side paths, NPC chatter, puzzles, boss, settlement. Keeps the main objective, the key choices, and the final reward.
options.tactic.trainingStudy.label: Training / study scenes
options.tactic.trainingStudy.tooltip: Teacher lectures, protagonist grasps it, rival scoffs, practice, a few fails, epiphany, breakthrough. Compresses the teaching detail; keeps the hard-won insight and the ability change.
options.tactic.circularArguments.label: Circular arguments
options.tactic.circularArguments.tooltip: 'You can't go.' 'I must.' 'You'll die.' 'Even so, I'll go.' Merges repeated positions; keeps the first clash, one escalation, and the decision.
options.tactic.leadingQuestions.label: Leading-question exposition
options.tactic.leadingQuestions.tooltip: 'What's this?' 'Dragon-Blood Pill.' 'Surely the legendary…?' — questions that bait a setting dump. Rewrites as natural short dialogue or narration.
options.tactic.rollCallStatements.label: Roll-call statements
options.tactic.rollCallStatements.toolti: In a meeting: A agrees, B opposes, C is neutral, D is snide, E slams the table, F is silent. Merges same-camp voices; keeps only the decisive lines.
options.tactic.repeatedConfirmations.too: 'What?' 'He broke through.' 'Really?' 'Really.' 'How?' Keeps only one effective reaction.
options.tactic.climaxPovSwitch.label: POV switch before the climax
options.tactic.climaxPovSwitch.tooltip: Right as the protagonist strikes, we cut to the villain, the onlookers, the love interest — back next chapter. If the new POV adds no key twist or danger, cut or move it.
options.tactic.multiPovReplay.label: Multi-POV replay
options.tactic.multiPovReplay.tooltip: One event retold from the protagonist, villain, onlooker, love-interest, and news POVs. Each POV must add new info or a new consequence; otherwise merge.
options.tactic.flashbacks.label: Flashbacks
options.tactic.flashbacks.tooltip: Childhood, the master's past, the first love, the old family case, a previous life, the war. Keeps only the fragments needed to explain the current choice or conflict.
options.tactic.dreamIllusionTrial.label: Dreams / illusions / trials
options.tactic.dreamIllusionTrial.toolti: Inner demons, past-life dreams, reincarnation trials, realm-illusions, mindscape. Keeps only what reveals fear/desire or delivers a key clue.
options.tactic.secretRealm.label: Secret realms / ruins
options.tactic.secretRealm.tooltip: Entry fights, rule dumps, traps, beasts, herbs, legacies, old rivals, the final treasure grab. Compresses repeated steps; keeps the core treasure and the protagonist's choices.
options.tactic.auction.label: Auctions
options.tactic.auction.tooltip: Entry snub, box tiers, auctioneer intro, item by item, bidding, the steal, the ambush. Details only the lots tied to the protagonist's goal or the main line.
options.tactic.entranceExam.label: Entrance exams / assessments
options.tactic.entranceExam.tooltip: Entry tests, talent / spiritual-root / mental / fitness tests, written, practical, interview, ranking. Keeps only the steps that sort ability or decide resource allocation.
options.tactic.hiddenPowerLoops.label: Repeated 'hidden power' reveals
options.tactic.hiddenPowerLoops.tooltip: Every new map: 'sneered at — provoked — effortless strike — shocks the room.' Keeps the most representative one; accelerates the rest.
options.tactic.identityReveals.label: Repeated identity reveals
options.tactic.identityReveals.tooltip: Miracle doctor, hacker, heiress, war god, award-winner — each mask peeled for another round of shock. Each reveal must bring a new plot consequence.
options.tactic.nobodyKnowsMc.label: 'Nobody knows who the MC is'
options.tactic.nobodyKnowsMc.tooltip: Clerks, classmates, relatives, villains, bosses, the fiancée's family — no one recognizes the protagonist; a fresh face-slap every scene. Keeps only the ones who actually block the protagonist's goal.
options.tactic.rankingBoards.label: Ranking boards
options.tactic.rankingBoards.tooltip: Talent rankings, wealth, combat power, pill-master boards, star-heat charts — a whole chapter to publish, plus reactions. Shows only ranks tied to the protagonist and core rivals.
options.tactic.rewardSettlement.label: Reward settlement
options.tactic.rewardSettlement.tooltip: Points, rank changes, rewards, achievements, votes, mentor feedback, fan growth, commercial value. Keeps only the biggest changes and what's useful downstream.
options.tactic.heiressDrama.label: True / fake heiress drama
options.tactic.heiressDrama.tooltip: True heiress returns, fake heiress plays victim, parents favor her, brother misjudges, banquet mishap, talent face-slap, family regrets. Compresses repeated grievance and misunderstanding.
options.tactic.evilSidekick.label: Evil side-chick scheming
options.tactic.evilSidekick.tooltip: Faked falls, framing theft, stealing credit, playing victim, buying shills, engineering misunderstandings. Keeps the new scheme and the counter; cuts repeated scheming.
options.tactic.ceoControlMinutiae.label: CEO control-freak minutiae
options.tactic.ceoControlMinutiae.toolti: Arranging drivers, clothes, meals, bodyguards; buying buildings and shops; tracking movements; jealous cold shoulders. Keeps only the details that show relationship tension or power conflict.
options.tactic.cuteBabyAssist.label: Cute-baby assists
options.tactic.cuteBabyAssist.tooltip: The cute baby misreads the leads' relationship, plays matchmaker, fakes sick, acts adorable, confirms paternity, genius-skill face-slaps. Keeps only what advances the relationship or the identity truth.
options.tactic.varietyLivestream.label: Variety / livestream tasks
options.tactic.varietyLivestream.tooltip: Guests arrive, split into teams, cook, play games, get interviewed; danmaku, anti-fans, trending topics, shippers, the directors' reactions. Keeps the rules, the conflict, and the public-opinion fallout.
options.tactic.engagementHumiliation.too: Humiliated, swears an oath, trains, fights, face-slap, the other side regrets, a bigger faction arrives. Keeps the core conflict and the oath; cuts the overlong mockery.
options.tactic.recruitingMinions.label: Recruiting minions
options.tactic.recruitingMinions.tooltip: The recruit resists, sees the protagonist's power, is shocked, swears allegiance, background dumped, his family trouble, protagonist solves it. Compresses the 'resist then bow' loop.
options.tactic.haremRotation.label: Rotating harem / love interests
options.tactic.haremRotation.tooltip: A new love interest every map, different backgrounds, all special to the protagonist, existing interests get jealous. Keeps only interactions that affect the main line or relationship structure.
options.tactic.treasureAppraisal.label: Treasure-appraisal pick-ups
options.tactic.treasureAppraisal.tooltip: Browsing the market, vendor hypes it, onlookers mock, protagonist spots the real deal, buys cheap, expert appraises, value jumps. Keeps the spot and the reveal.
options.tactic.medicalRescue.label: Miracle-doctor rescues
options.tactic.medicalRescue.tooltip: Patient critical, famous doctors stumped, family doubts, protagonist steps in, explains needles/prescription, recovery, awe. Compresses repeated doubt; keeps the crisis and the key treatment.
options.tactic.techSpecs.label: Tech-spec lectures
options.tactic.techSpecs.tooltip: Ship models, engine principles, weapon output, power systems, AI logic, gene-mod mechanics. Keeps only the parameters that affect choices or outcomes.
options.tactic.apocalypseSupplies.label: Apocalypse supply lists
options.tactic.apocalypseSupplies.toolti: Rice, flour, oil, meds, weapons, fuel, generators, water purifiers, seeds, cans, cold-weather gear. Keeps only the scarce items that shape survival strategy.
options.tactic.baseBuilding.label: Base-building
options.tactic.baseBuilding.tooltip: Walls, room assignment, rules, recruiting, supply tallies, defenses, farming, internal friction. Keeps the build decisions and resource conflicts.
options.tactic.instanceRules.label: Instance rule dumps
options.tactic.instanceRules.tooltip: Instance backstory, clear conditions, taboos, NPC settings, time limits, reward/penalty mechanics. Keeps only the rules that will be used or that backfire if broken.
options.tactic.puzzleTrialError.label: Puzzle trial-and-error
options.tactic.puzzleTrialError.tooltip: Find a clue, scrap the theory, re-discuss, another clue, players argue, protagonist broods, the reveal. Merges dead-end guesses; keeps the key clues and the conclusion.
options.tactic.corporateMeetings.label: Corporate-battle meetings
options.tactic.corporateMeetings.tooltip: Market analysis, shareholder fights, investor pressure, competitor moves, financials, PR plans, legal risk. Keeps only the decision conflicts and the protagonist's key calls.
options.tactic.projectCompetition.label: Project / wager competition
options.tactic.projectCompetition.toolti: Two teams compete, plans clash, boss plays favorites, colleagues sabotage, clients push back, protagonist turns it around. Keeps the goal, the obstacle, the breakthrough, and the result.
options.tactic.actingAudition.label: Acting / auditions
options.tactic.actingAudition.tooltip: Script intro, character interpretation, director's doubt, rival's provocation, protagonist finds the role, awe, trending explosion. Keeps the role's difficulty and the performance breakthrough.
options.tactic.fandomWars.label: Fandom fan-wars
options.tactic.fandomWars.tooltip: Fans fight over billing, hype accounts stir it, rivals plant hit pieces, the studio statement, shippers, anti-fans meltdown. Keeps the opinion shift and the career impact.
options.tactic.chapterRecap.label: Previous-chapter recap
options.tactic.chapterRecap.tooltip: New chapter opens recapping what just happened, how strong the enemy is, how shocked everyone was, how dire the protagonist's situation is. Cut or crush to one line unless truly needed.
options.tactic.forcedCliffhanger.label: Forced cliffhangers
options.tactic.forcedCliffhanger.tooltip: 'And yet, the true crisis was only beginning.' 'Outside the door, a familiar voice.' Cuts empty cliffhangers; if kept, requires a concrete new signal.
options.tactic.synonymStacking.label: Synonym stacking
options.tactic.synonymStacking.tooltip: 'He was angry. Angrier than ever. Rage that would burn reason to ash.' Crushes three samey lines into the strongest one.
options.tactic.adjectivePiling.label: Adjective piling
options.tactic.adjectivePiling.tooltip: 'A cold, terrifying, grim, oppressive, suffocating aura.' Keeps the one or two most accurate words; swaps the rest for action or result.
options.tactic.atmosphereRedressing.tool: Overcast skies, howling wind, flickering candles, thick air, killing intent. Compresses when it doesn't affect anyone's action or judgment.
options.tactic.numberPiling.label: Number-piling
options.tactic.numberPiling.tooltip: A hundred materials, thirty-six steps, ninety-nine peaks, a hundred thousand troops. Keeps only the numbers that affect scale, difficulty, or a choice.
options.tactic.mapProgressionTemplate.to: Every new map repeats 'sneered at — provoke a minor villain — beat him — provoke a bigger one — level up — next map.' Compresses the repeated front half; a new map must bring new rules or a new conflict.
options.tactic.escalatingCrisis.label: Crisis to fix to bigger-crisis loop
options.tactic.escalatingCrisis.tooltip: Beat the beasts, the realm collapses; escape the enemy, they're at the gate; join the sect, there's a mole. Each crisis must carry a cost or a character change.
options.tactic.infinitePrep.label: Infinite prep phases
options.tactic.infinitePrep.tooltip: Before the battle / wedding / match / exam: gear, meds, plans, formations, pep talks, the villain's own prep. Keeps only the prep that shapes the outcome; starts the real event sooner.
options.tactic.waitingForResults.label: Waiting for results
options.tactic.waitingForResults.tooltip: Waiting on the test, the ranking, the verdict, the doctor, the system settlement, the legacy's approval. Compresses the waiting psyche and chatter; publishes the result sooner.
options.tactic.palaceEtiquette.label: Palace drama: etiquette & rewards
options.tactic.palaceEtiquette.tooltip: Daily greetings, ranks, reward lists, palace rules, messages passed, seating, bows. Keeps only the etiquette that shows a power shift or a trap.
options.tactic.householdAccounts.label: Household drama: accounts & stewardship
options.tactic.householdAccounts.tooltip: Auditing accounts, running the shops, monthly allowances, disciplining servants, skimmed silver, dowry lists, main vs. branch rules. Keeps only the key accounting problems and interest conflicts.
options.tactic.farmingRoutine.label: Farming routine
options.tactic.farmingRoutine.tooltip: Tilling, sowing, watering, fertilizing, harvesting, cooking, market day, selling, building. Keeps the steps that show a change in yield or livelihood; summarizes the rest.
options.tactic.eraFictionCoupons.label: Era fiction: coupons & neighbors
options.tactic.eraFictionCoupons.tooltip: Grain coupons, cloth coupons, work-points, courtyard neighbors, factory commendations, matchmaking, busybody chatter. Keeps what shows the era's constraints and resource conflicts.
options.tactic.cthulhuDelaying.label: Cthulhu / mystery: 'indescribable' delay
options.tactic.cthulhuDelaying.tooltip: Indescribable dread, incomprehensible whispers, eerie sigils, a sense of being watched, 'something's off.' Keeps only the description that forms a clue or escalates the dread.
